newsitem.title: NORWAY: NORDIC SKIING-YEGOROVA FIGHTS BACK AS RUSSIA KEEP SPOTLIGHT.
newsitem.headline: NORDIC SKIING-YEGOROVA FIGHTS BACK AS RUSSIA KEEP SPOTLIGHT.

text.p: Lyubov Yegorova proved she was back at her brilliant best by narrowly beating Yelena Vialbe into second place in the 5-km classical style cross-country race on Sunday as Russia kept the spotlight at the Nordic skiing world championships.

Yegorova, who had been struggling to recapture her best form since winning three gold medals at the Lillehammer Olympics three years ago, was 0.6 seconds slower than fellow Russian Vialbe after 1.8 km but a strong finish allowed her to clock a winning time of 13 minutes 29.90 seconds.
Vialbe, who won the opening 15-km freestyle race on Friday, had to be content with second place in 13:32.70 to add a 13th world championship medal to her collection.
Stefania Belmondo, who was second to Vialbe on Friday, had to admit Russia's dominance once again as she came third in 13:35.00.
Yegorova began to hope for a win when she learned she would start 62nd, as she did when she won gold over the same distance in the 1994 Olympics.
"I thought it was a good sign," she said. "I was feeling in great shape and then I found my skis had been very well prepared. Everything was just perfect."
After Lillehammer, Yegorova retired from competition to give birth to a boy, Viktor. She then experienced health problems and started wondering if she would ever make it back to the top.
"It was particularly difficult because I'm not that young," said the 30-year-old Russian, whose best result this winter was a third place last month before her home fans in Kavagolovo.
Yegorova and Vialbe will go for more in Monday's 10-km race, the second part of a pursuit event which started with Sunday's race.

Belmondo, who said before the start of the 10-day championships that she would search for gold in every competition she entered, promised to keep trying in Monday's race, which she will start with a 5.1-second handicap on Yegorova.
"There's only one tactic and that is to start strong and keep going, hoping the two Russian girls will crack," she said. "Or maybe they will celebrate and drink too much vodka. That would help."
Yegorova smiled but hinted she was not ready to do her Italian rival any favours.
"It's so good to be winning again," she said. "Let's hope it will continue."
